findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime fields
findings.body: The endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `get_item_key` calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on the attribute value. Since the `datetime` field on `AuditLogEntry` is a Python `datetime` object, this will raise `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`. The existing `DateTimePaginator` correctly converts via `float(value.strftime("%s.%f")) * self.multiplier` before applying floor/ceil. This paginator will crash on every request that uses the optimized path.

findings.title: Negative offset passed to Django queryset slicing raises AssertionError
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` (a negative integer) and then slices the queryset with `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django's QuerySet does not support negative indexing and will raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The comment claiming 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually incorrect. Since cursor offset is parsed from user-supplied input via `Cursor.from_string()` with no lower-bound validation, any authenticated admin can trigger a 500 error by crafting a cursor string with a negative offset.

findings.title: BasePaginator change removes offset clamping for is_prev across all subclasses
findings.body: The change from `queryset[offset:stop]` to `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` means that when `cursor.is_prev` is True, the offset is used without clamping to zero. Since `Cursor.from_string()` parses user input with `int(bits[1])` and performs no non-negativity check, a malicious or malformed cursor string with a negative offset and `is_prev=1` will pass a negative value to queryset slicing in every `BasePaginator` subclass (DateTimePaginator, Paginator, etc.), causing an AssertionError. This is a regression affecting all existing paginators, not just the new one.

findings.title: No validation that cursor offset is non-negative allows user-controlled negative values
findings.body: The `Cursor.__init__` accepts any integer for `offset` (via `int(offset)`) and `Cursor.from_string` parses user-supplied cursor strings without validating that the offset component is >= 0. Combined with the paginator changes in this PR that use offset values directly in queryset slicing, this allows an attacker to inject negative offsets. Even without the paginator changes, negative offsets could cause unexpected behavior in cursor comparison logic (e.g., `_build_next_values` and `_build_prev_values` arithmetic). A guard like `self.offset = max(0, int(offset))` or raising `BadPaginationError` for negative values would be appropriate.

findings.title: Authorization check uses has_global_access which may be broader than intended
findings.body: The condition `organization_context.member.has_global_access` grants access to the 'optimized' paginator path for any member with global access (typically org owners, managers, and admins). The PR description and comments frame this as an admin-only feature, but `has_global_access` is a broader permission level. If the intent is truly superuser-only, the check should be `request.user.is_superuser` alone. If the broader access is intentional, the security rationale in the comments ('permissions are checked at the queryset level') is misleading since the queryset is already filtered to the organization—the gate here is about enabling a buggy code path, not about data access.

findings.title: Non-advanced path in OptimizedCursorPaginator still allows unclamped offset for is_prev
findings.body: In the else branch (line 884), `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` replicates the same problematic pattern from BasePaginator. When `cursor.is_prev` is True and offset is negative (possible via user-crafted cursor strings), this passes a negative value to queryset slicing, causing a crash. The 'advanced features' gate only controls one branch; the fallback branch has the same vulnerability.
